rows.requirement: Everyday coding in Subfleet instead of the Claude and Codex apps, with both providers
A conversation moves to an account with capacity; no manual sign-in/out between accounts
rows.notes: Claude: automatic, with labelled continuation after a limit and account affinity otherwise. Codex: pinned to its home; moves by labelled handoff unless the Stage 3 relocation test passes. Daemon side: usage-limit failover with a labelled continuation on another lane, same session (tests/e2e/test_conversations.py).

rows.requirement: Existing Claude and Codex sessions appear under their display names
Clicking an existing Claude session opens it and lets him continue it
Clicking an existing Codex-app thread opens it and lets him continue it
rows.notes: History plus labelled handoff; in-place continuation only if the Stage 3 relocation test passes (design §15, §16).

rows.requirement: A normal macOS app: window controls, Dock, menus, not an overlay
Menu bar bolt keeps the quota popover and an obvious Open action
Return sends; Shift-Return inserts a newline
Paste screenshots and images into the composer and send them
Composer stays editable while a turn runs; follow-ups queue
Local acknowledgement p95 <= 250 ms; activity shown within 1 s of an event
Submit to provider acknowledgement and to first output, p50/p95, within 1.5 s of the native app's p95 for new and resumed conversations on each provider
rows.notes: Measured in Stage 3 beside the native app on the same account; a miss reopens warm workers.

rows.requirement: Shows what the agent is thinking and doing, live
Markdown renders in conversations
Fast is its own setting, independent of model and reasoning effort
rows.notes: Claude Fast bills usage credits; labelled and confirmed per conversation.

rows.requirement: Per-account usage: percent, reset times, weekly reset, Fable/overall/5-hour windows
Project selection and compose with workspace choice, settings and errors
Model, reasoning and Fast controls negotiated against the provider catalog; unsupported settings never implied
Real permission and question requests with allow/deny/answer/cancel round trips in Subfleet
rows.notes: Daemon side done: tests/e2e/test_conversations.py approval, question, deny, person-only refusal, duplicate answer, restart mid-approval. App side pending.

rows.requirement: Cancel a queued message; stop only the owned active turn
rows.notes: Daemon side: turn.interrupt and the unblock note have e2e tests; message.cancel e2e pending.

rows.requirement: Changes and results per turn and per conversation, tied to workspace and attempt; no automatic commit or merge
Bounded read-only history of existing sessions; IDs preserved
Explicit cross-provider handoff with provenance, never presented as the same session
Truthful fleet/status; reloading a snapshot is not a new observation
Drafts and attachments survive app restart
Compose and dispatch detached jobs with a route preview (kept from the legacy cockpit)
Follow-ups keep the conversation's model, effort, Fast and permission settings
A capability the daemon does not offer is disabled with its reason
Notifications when a background conversation completes, fails or needs approval
Lost acknowledgement, app restart, daemon recovery and ambiguous sends: no duplicate accepted turn, no automatic re-send
rows.notes: Daemon side: kill -9 mid-approval adopts the turn and sends nothing twice (tests/e2e/test_conversations.py). App outbox pending.

rows.requirement: Independent conversations; external-writer handling; single writer per session
Explicit endpoint; no v1 fallback; daemon-down is a visible state
Guard, trust and toolchain pins pass for every turn launch, including the Codex turn server
rows.notes: Daemon: a Codex turn launches only with the verified guard override and re-checks hooks/list on its own server (codex_turn.check_hooks); e2e with the fake app-server in tests/e2e/test_conversations.py. Live app-server firing test pending.

rows.requirement: Real isolated Claude and Codex task with response, served-model evidence and a useful diff
Installed release: exact source/build hashes, CI evidence, rollback bundle, guardian adoption verified
Backend and UI rollback rehearsed on a copy; the main store stays schema 5
rows.notes: design §11 Recovery: drain turn jobs before a daemon rollback.

rows.requirement: Capacity waiting, fleet-full, daemon down, auth failure, stale usage, unsupported setting and model mismatch are distinguishable from completion
Legacy cockpit import: repeated import creates nothing new; every legacy message has an owner and disposition
evidence: tests/unit/test_importer.py, legacy cockpit section: per-message classification, repeated import creates nothing, held sessions, client journal, dry run, daemon.lock
tests/unit/test_conversation_store.py: legacy history is terminal, idempotent by id, written first, never dispatched
tests/e2e/test_legacy_cockpit.py: imported history reopens through the daemon by its native session, and a new message resumes that session while no history row is sent

tests/unit/test_legacy_hold.py: the import's hold keeps every turn off its conversation (no dispatch, no re-admission, no admission of a queued turn job, a running turn stopped on adoption), and no outcome, unblock or resolve replaces or lifts it
rows.notes: Not run against the real v1 state yet. A dry run over a private copy of the real outbox (2026-09-24, scratch state root) placed all 6 finished messages as history in 3 legacy conversations. A real pass needs the daemon stopped (docs/migration.md, 'The legacy cockpit, milestone 9').

Legacy delivery state inventoried privately; every pending message has an owner and disposition
